package.question: Do the Amharic-specific Model M encoders retrieve passages more effectively than general-purpose multilingual embedding models, and does any advantage carry over to a different Amharic test collection?
package.methods_summary: Model M is a family of three Amharic dense bi-encoder retrievers (40M, 42M and 110M parameters) built on Amharic BERT/RoBERTa encoders with a 512-token context. They are trained on Amharic query-passage pairs with a multiple-negatives ranking loss (4 epochs, sentence-transformers). Baselines are general-purpose multilingual embedding models used without Amharic fine-tuning: gte-modernbert-base, gte-multilingual-base, multilingual-e5-large-instruct and snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2.0.
package.experimental_setup: Main data: an Amharic passage retrieval set built from an Amharic news classification corpus, using each headline as a query and its article body as the only relevant passage (about 45K pairs after de-duplication; 10% held out, stratified by news category). Model M is trained on the remaining 90%. Metrics: MRR@k, NDCG@k (binary relevance) and Recall@k. Generalization: zero-shot evaluation on 2AIRTC, a separate TREC-style Amharic collection with manually assessed topics. Significance for the main table uses a paired t-test; no seeds or variance are reported.

source_passages.text: 2AIRTC, a TREC-style test collection for standardized Amharic IR evaluation, but it lacks baseline retrieval benchmarks and complete relevance judgments, making recall-based assessments unreliable.
